_: The single source of truth for everything that identifies this app.
Nothing else in the project should hardcode a name, a version or an
identifier. Change a value here, run `npm run config` in mobile/, and it is
written into brand.js, manifest.json, index.html, capacitor.config.json,
the iOS Info.plist, the Android strings.xml and both store listings.
The two names are deliberate. `sweary` is what the app calls itself with
the swearing setting on, which is how it ships and how it is meant to be
read. `clean` is a name in its own right for when the setting is off — and,
as things stand, the name the shops will accept. See store.name below.
tagline: A proper weather app that tells you exactly what the sky is doing, then takes the mickey out of it.

_: PROFANITY WARNING — READ BEFORE SUBMITTING.
`name` here is the name that goes on the App Store and Google Play. It is
set to the clean twin, not because anybody decided to rename the app, but
because Apple review guideline 1.1.1 and the Google Play inappropriate-
content policy both refuse profanity in a public listing name, and both
shops surface app names to under-18 accounts regardless of age rating.
Submitting as `Fucking Weather` is very likely a rejection, and a rejected
name costs a review cycle each time.
The app is unaffected: with swearing on, which is the default, it calls
itself Fucking Weather everywhere inside — header, About, share card.
Only the shop front is clean.
To ship under the sweary name anyway, set this to name.sweary and rerun
`npm run config`. Nothing else needs touching.
store.name: Blooming Weather
store.subtitle: The forecast, with an attitude

support._: Both shops require a working support contact and will reject a listing without one. Nobody can fill these in but you — put in an address you actually read.
